Topic: Principles of Holography and Diffraction: Capturing Light in 3D

Target audience: University students (Physics/Engineering majors)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light

Lecture lines:
Light travels as an oscillating wave.
Superposition creates constructive interference peaks.
Phase encodes the information.

Planned animations:
Create a light source dot (white) in center.
Animate outward circular waves (cyan) from source.
Display two slits (yellow) vertically at right.
Show waves passing through slits, forming patterns.
Highlight overlap region (magenta) where interference occurs.

Section: section_2 — The Mechanism of Diffraction

Lecture lines:
Light spreads upon hitting obstacles.
Huygens-Fresnel principle defines this scattering.
Diffraction is an object's signature.

Planned animations:
Place a point light source (white) on left.
Animate plane waves (cyan) hitting an obstacle.
Show waves bending around obstacle edges (orange).

Section: section_3 — Recording the Hologram (The Interference Pattern)

Lecture lines:
Split laser into two beams.
Reference and Object beams interact.
Interference pattern forms on film.
This acts as complex grating.
Grid stores 3D object data.

Planned animations:
Show reference beam (blue) hitting film.
Show object beam (green) reflecting from object.
Overlay beam patterns on film surface (white).

Section: section_4 — Reconstruction: Decoding the Diffraction

Lecture lines:
Reference beam strikes developed hologram.
Diffraction reconstructs original wavefronts.
Floating 3D ghost appears.
Light mimics the object source.
Visual depth is perfectly preserved.

Planned animations:
Project reference beam (blue) onto developed hologram.
Show light diffracting out from film (yellow).
Visualize virtual 3D image forming (green).

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Holography stores complex diffraction patterns.
Secures credit card data.
Enables advanced AR displays.

Planned animations:
Flash hologram icon (red) at center.
Slide security credit card (magenta) onto screen.
Fade out all with final label text.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
